title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 122
paragraphs: The cause of Polycrates' death is told in these two different ways; we may believe whichever we please. Oroetes, who had his residence at the Magnesia situated on the river Maeander, sent Myrsos son of Gyges, a Lydian, to Samos bearing a message, having perceived Polycrates' designs. For Polycrates was the first of the Hellenes we know of who set his mind on command of the sea, apart from Minos the Cnossian and any other who may have ruled the sea before him. Of what we call the mortal race, Polycrates was the first, and he had great expectations of becoming ruler of Ionia and the islands. Oroetes, therefore, having perceived this design of his, sent him a message as follows: “Oroetes to Polycrates says this: I hear that you are making plans for great power, and that your wealth does not match your ambitions. Now, therefore, if you will do as I say, you will both do well for yourself and save me from destruction. For King Cambyses is planning my death, and this has been reported to me beyond all doubt. Take me and my wealth out of danger; keep a portion for yourself and let me keep a portion, and then, so far as wealth can bring it about, you shall be ruler of all Hellas. And if you do not believe what I say about the money, send someone you trust most, and I will show it to him.”
